variants.when: 2014–2016 S60, S80, V60, XC60 and XC70 (service message in the instrument cluster)
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have been changed (or the scheduled service was done).
Switch the ignition to position I without starting the engine. On keyless cars, press START briefly without touching the brake.
Press and hold the OK button on the end of the left steering-column stalk.
Keep holding it and switch the ignition to position II. On keyless cars, hold START for about 2 to 3 seconds, still without the brake.
Keep holding OK for about 10 seconds until the information light starts to flash, then let go. A chime confirms the reset.
Switch the ignition off and leave it off for at least 3 minutes so the car's modules shut down normally.
variants.note: If the message does not clear, repeat the steps while holding the RESET button on the same stalk together with OK; repair technicians report that OK alone does not always work.

variants.when: C30 and other P1-platform cars (S40, V50, C70) with a key ignition
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have been changed (or the scheduled service was done).
Turn the key to position I without starting the engine.
Press and hold the trip meter reset button.
Keep holding it, turn the key to position II, and let go when the amber information light flashes. A chime confirms the reset.

variants.when: Models with the Car Status app on the center touchscreen (checked on 2018–2019 XC40, XC60, XC90, S60 and S90)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the tire placard on the driver's door pillar, with the car switched off. These cars have no monitored spare.
Start the car and leave it parked with the engine running. The button you need only works while the car is standing still.
On the center display, open the Car Status app from App view and tap TPMS.
Tap Calibrate (on cars built from about late 2018 the button may read Store pressure), then tap OK to confirm you checked all four tires.
Drive normally above about 22 mph (35 km/h). The system learns the new pressures while you drive; the tire symbols on the screen turn from gray to green when it has enough data.
Let it finish in the same drive. If you switch off before it completes, do the steps again.
variants.note: This is an indirect system: until new pressures are stored it cannot warn correctly, so repeat this after every tire change or pressure adjustment. If the screen says storing was unsuccessful, try again. If the tire pressure symbol flashes for about a minute and then stays on, the system has a fault that this procedure will not clear; have it checked by a qualified shop.

variants.when: Older models with tire pressure sensors in the wheels (for example the 2016 S80)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the tire placard on the driver's door pillar.
Drive for several minutes at 20 mph (30 km/h) or faster. The warning clears and the light goes out on its own; there is no reset button.

notes: On Volvos from about 2016 on (XC90, then the other redesigned models) the service message tells you to contact a workshop, and the owner's manual pages we checked give no driver reset for it. Newer Volvo tire pressure systems must store new pressures after every inflation or tire change.
